changes.evidence: The handwritten top-centre numeral has a hooked 2 and a double-loop 8. The scan marker 29 is editorial metadata, not a second handwritten number.

The proposition crop shows an upright with a long curved upper arm and a separate shorter middle arm. Its shape agrees with the ordinary F forms elsewhere on this sheet; no distinct script alphabet is indicated. The entire surrounding F et G pour << formula was read.
The short word is a low o followed by n. There is neither a preceding q descender nor an apostrophe. The separately rubbed glyph belongs immediately before the following live l’appelle.

A small rubbed or cancelled vertical/descending ink form remains before the clear live l of l’appelle. Its upper fork can belong to y, while the reduced stem can also be l. It is not sufficiently plain to settle under deletion.
The opening and closing marks are pairs of short strokes. No angular guillemets are drawn.
A horizontal underline lies below the heading. Bold type does not encode this physical underline.
The line below n’est pas is an underline, separate from the insertion leader farther right.

The insertion crop shows separated en, a descending g-loop, an accent over the following compressed e-run, and the final tall l. The curved leader joins the gap before la figure. The insertion is live.
The stroke above la figure curves up toward the inserted en général. It is an insertion leader and does not run as a cancellation through the words; the letters remain live.

The tall shaft, polygonal upper outline and low curl survive clearly, but do not settle the typeset alphabet. C’s candidates are retained at the first occurrence on the page, and the first candidate is used at the repeated cancelled occurrence. This is retained uncertainty rather than a lexical correction.

changes.place: warning, L in cancelled G subset P(L)

changes.place: warning, after cancelled G subset P(L)

The article shows a tall l and a low open e-exit. There is no closed a-oval.

The first short word has the c/cedilla stroke and a closed a; the following word has the tall h toward its right and ends with an e-exit. Neither the extra syllables nor the terminal t of construit are present.

The initial thin vertical has a lower leftward curl, favouring s over l, but the retraced strokes do not exclude the tall-stem reading. The remainder apparente is readable. H’s alternative is retained in place; grammar was not used to remove the doubt.

changes.place: footer, nested cancellation after first F
changes.evidence: Two horizontal strikes conceal much of the short phrase. A comma-like curve, crossing t-like form, and taller d-like stroke survive, but not every letter; the whole candidate remains doubtful. A separate live comma after this cancelled phrase is retained before alors.

The crop gives a barred capital I, the two compressed m groups, accented é, tall looped d, short i mark, a lower a join and terminal tall t. There is no terminal e after t. The diagonal cancellation does not obscure these letter parts.
The crop shows s-u, two distinct p descenders, the low or run, a tall crossed t, and a low terminal s-exit. The strike is diagonal and can be separated from these strokes.

changes.evidence: The apparent descending p-stem is the long diagonal cancellation that continues through the whole footer. The surviving initial curved s and the following low u/r match the sur in the preceding parenthesis; no closed a bowl is present.

notes: Source is a handwritten portrait sheet. No diagram, drawing, marginal note, typescript or separate archive number was observed.
Manuscript page number is 28. Scan marker 29 is editorial metadata and is not counted as a handwritten numeral.

The proposition calls the constructed Inf of F and G for << the figure intersection F.G. The warning says this need not be the set intersection F cap G in general; the following compatibility sentence and support display were transcribed without mathematical repair.
The sentence where F et G compatibles has no visible sont. Both witnesses omit it; none is supplied.
The cancelled footer asserts the displayed subdivision relation and calls the subdivision induced on a refinement. Its assertion remains cancelled in full, even though its text is readable.
No mathematical proof or external consistency check was performed. All decisions here are visual readings and local comparisons of ink; check_events is consequently empty.
H’s final note that the proposition is crossed out is editorial description, not words on the manuscript. It is not transcribed.
Physical line count: 22 main, cancelled and display baselines, plus one supralinear insertion baseline. The isolated page number is not included in line_count 23.
No numerical indices occur apart from the manuscript page number. The support display uses dotted i and capital I, not the digit 1.
The H_marked flag is true for H’s explicit uncertain or illegible reading at the locus. Its editorial statement about cancellation is described separately and is not treated as a doubt mark.

A first attempted top-right header crop contained no ink and was discarded. The retained page_number evidence is the inspected top-centre header crop. It was not recropped after the numeral was settled.

The ordinary-word blank line before Nous in the proposed text follows C’s division. The handwriting has ordinary line spacing there; no claim of a new indented paragraph is made from the spacing alone.
